claim_reviews.conclusion: “Medical check-up” appropriately cues a routine examination of a person’s health; the sense is aligned.
claim_reviews.subject: English cue and sense

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Cek kesehatan” is an established everyday Indonesian expression, but “pemeriksaan kesehatan” is also an accepted formal equivalent.
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian answer

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Pemeriksaan kesihatan” is an established Malaysian Malay term for medical examination/health inspection and is suitable for the intended sense.
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian answer

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Different-common-word” is too strong without a register qualifier. The formal Indonesian expression “pemeriksaan kesehatan” and Malaysian “pemeriksaan kesihatan” are ordinary cognate equivalents, differing mainly in spelling; Malaysian terminology also maps English “check-up” to “pemeriksaan.”
claim_reviews.subject: National split and relation

claim_reviews.conclusion: No contrast is supplied. A qualified contrast would be useful: Indonesian “cek” is an everyday check/examination form, whereas Malaysian “cek” primarily denotes a cheque but also has a colloquial inspect sense; this is not an absolute false friend.
claim_reviews.subject: False-friend contrast

response.rationale: Both answers express the intended sense, but the national split is materially overstated. Indonesian also uses the formal equivalent “pemeriksaan kesehatan,” while Malaysian Malay standard terminology includes “pemeriksaan kesihatan”; “cek” additionally exists in Malaysian Malay as a colloquial verb meaning to inspect. The relation should be revised or qualified by register. The empty contrast field also misses a useful, but non-absolute, cek/cek distinction.
